chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Drummer Quank and other drummers shifting between bands
summary: Details of who drummed for Superior and Olympia bands, and Foster's moving between jobs and dances.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Dave, Dave play climate, Dave DePass, and Arnall, he was very good, see, but a drummer, we wanted another drummer, so, we got Quank, known as Ernest Prakhan, we call him Quank, see,

So, Quank would play with us all the week, now, then he played on a Sunday, because we were waiting this week, on a Sunday, he played with, with the Olympic band, but our record drummer was working in the Jewish store, when he played with us on Sundays, on a record drummer, see? Now, Henry Martin played with the Olympic band through the week, with all the outside jobs, Quank played them, see? And we were waiting, see, like, I feel like I want to, you feel like you want to change. I'd slip off and go on over to Billy Phillips, and, and, and, and, then they had, he had, Billy Marrero was over there, with him for a while, and John Lindsay. Well, they'd come over to play in my place, I'd go over there. Now, when I get tired of playing down there, I used to lay off on a Saturday night, they'd go play with the Eagle Band, to play some different music, some blues or something. Now, nobody, they'd notice it was your layoff, and I used to get off, and get off at night, we'd get off at 12 o'clock, and I'd run, when we get off, sometimes I'm going to get off all night, I'd run like a dicks to get up there, and dance at Cross Hill, by the Cross Hill, and I used to get a kick out of that Cross Hill, looking at them guys dancing. Just, just, now we, like, if you, you walk in a place like, Manion, say, Manion, you'll be playing, violin, piano, whatever you'll be playing, Manion, play this number for Manion, see? Guys say, can't play till Manion, come back. If he didn't come back, he'd stay there one night. Manion, there was nothing said, the leader didn't say nothing.
